reviews.t: Not great at first but now I like it
reviews.x: I really struggled with this nail stamper at first. It did not work out of the box for me like it did for other reviewers. This is essentially what worked for me.  1.  I washed  the stamper head with dish soap. After it dried, I did a very light swipe of rubbing alcohol. This will be the only time I ever treat it with anything but soap and water (in order to protect the ability to see through the stamper). 2.  The stamper head is very squishy. This makes it a dream for transferring images onto y
Love this stamper....transfers excellent. Love how you can see thru it also, to help with positioning.

reviews.t: which works better because it has an open end
reviews.x: Mine came broken, but I didn't mind because I just put the jelly part in a different clear handle, which works better because it has an open end, unlike this one that is covered in clear plastic. I like that it has a cap, but I guess I would just recommend buying the one with the an open end. I also use an old debit card as a scrapper. I don't use this card, but I'm guessing it works better than the plastic / metal razor looking ones that others come with.

I was not a fan of this stamper at all. It did not pick up the images from the stamping plate. I tried cleaning the tip, cleaning the stamp plate, used thin and thick nail polish and nothing worked. The only thing I liked about this was that you could see the image and where it would be placed if it actually picked it up. I do not recommend this. It is worth spending a little more money for something that picks up an image.

Once I received it, I used it!  It works great! I'm not a seasoned stamper as I've only done it a couple times, but this has been great to use.  It's very flexible and easy to clean. You can view the image you picked up from all sides. Top, side, bottom. I love that I can see the image and where I will be stamping it before stamping my finger. reviews.t: Works as described, had practiced with it because I ...
reviews.x: Works as described, had practiced with it because I had trouble picking up the stamp. Don't use acetone polish on stamper bc it will make image cloudy, I had to lightly file stamper head to get image to show up. You can use clear tape or lint roller to remove excess polish from the stammer head after you have stamped your design on your nail.

I like it. I was trying to find out how to buff the clear top. I find out got used nail sander on the smooth size to buff to top nail stamping. It work. Nail polish on the plate got be a lot and scrap it light.

reviews.x: Love it but be careful with yours - mine tore already! Still love it, though!!!!!
Was so excited to get my new stamp that I could see through but it does not pick up polish well at all. I do not recommend it.
It does not pick up the picture on the plate. Waste money
Polish never stuck to it so I can't use it

I wouldn't buy this ever again it doesn't pickup the stamping image at all and it's way to big so I've watched a few how to do stamping videos on u tube and it looks like the ones that are not jelly are the best ones to use if u want a good stamping image on ur nails and the fact that this one was cheep could have something to do with it also so I gotta buy some good ones like a pack of different kinds that way I can choose the right one for the image I'm trying to go for.

reviews.t: and I don't recommend it. The silicone does not pick up the ...
reviews.x: This was my first stamper, and I don't recommend it. The silicone does not pick up the paint unless you prime it first - you'll need to 'sand' it down with a nail file to give it texture so the paint will actually stick to it, but very carefully or the silicone will rip. The silicone is a little too soft and will only pick up wide designs from the plate. Invest in the more expensive sets with firmer pads that have some texture.

reviews.t: Jelly sinks into holder and smears nail art
reviews.x: The clear holder and jelly work great for seeing nail art placement, but when stamping, the jelly sinks sideways and often smears my stamp. Also it is not great for shallow etched plates - but that is the nature of squishy jelly and not a product fault. Will try glue to see if it works to hold the jelly in place.

Does not pick up the polish very well at all from the metal image plates. Very slipper surface on the transfer area. And it doesn't smoosh all the way into the cracks on the plate to even REACH the image, so it's not surprising. There's got to be a better method for this. Cause it's a really cool idea... [...]

the plastic got some acetone on it from my finger and it went cloudy and got my finger stuck to it! Then, trying to take off a stamp with a top coat over it off the head of the stamp with my RUBBER tool it tore the jelly in 2 different places. WAY too fragile.

As I find with most clear stampers, they work great at first, then it's hit or miss.  Same with this one, I like it, but the more you push, the stamper shoves up into the handle, you have to pull it back out.  I've used better ones, but this one is ok

Perfect for stamping. Picks up the patterns well and deposits them even better. Nice and soft and it really helps to be able to see through the stamper so that you can line up the stamp the way you want it.
Squishy but not too squishy. Arrived early and works exactly how i needed it too. I only prepped by washing it with water to get any production residue off. Love the cap that goes over the top.
Mine works great!  The only thing I did to prep it was wash gently with warm water and soap.  It grabs stamps  beautifully , and you can see exactly  how  to  get  a  good  placement.

This is a nice nail stamper.  I like that it is clear so you can see exactly where the design is going.  This does take some practice using as it is very flexible.
I didn't need to prime the stamper at all, it's started working right out of the package! It picks up really well. The price is nice for such a wonderful product!

claims.text: Many reviewers report the stamper fails to pick up polish or images from the stamping plate.
Reviewers like being able to see through the clear stamper to position the image.
Some reviewers say it works well once you prime or prep the silicone head (e.g., washing, filing, or sanding it).
A few reviewers mention the silicone is fragile, tearing or ripping easily.
Some reviewers note the jelly head sinks or smears during stamping.
